headline: East Hampton power surge leaves 41 homes awaiting electrical inspections
dek: Eversource crews and firefighters are checking wiring before service returns after a suspected equipment malfunction left residents without power and prompted smoke calls.
body: Eversource crews and East Hampton firefighters are going door to door after a possible power surge affected 41 homes in the Connecticut town, leaving residents waiting for electrical inspections before service can safely return. Town officials said the incident followed an Eversource equipment malfunction Tuesday night, Oct. 13, but the company and town have not described a final technical cause. The affected area includes Hog Hill Road, Terp Lane and Schoolhouse Lane, according to [WFSB’s report](https://www.wfsb.com/2026/10/14/power-surge-may-have-damaged-wiring-east-hampton-homes-town-says/).

The immediate concern is not simply the loss of electricity. Officials said the voltage event may have damaged wiring or circuits inside individual houses, creating a risk that power could be restored to a damaged system. The inspection process is therefore being handled home by home rather than as a routine outage repair. Eversource told WFSB that extensive testing of electrical equipment in the affected homes was required before service could safely resume.

East Hampton Town Manager David Cox told WFSB that at least 19 people called 911 Tuesday night after noticing some smoke inside their homes. The report said officials did not believe the damage was widespread, but at least one house had circuit problems that would require significant electrical work. Those details remain preliminary: the sources do not report a confirmed fire, injuries or a complete accounting of property damage.

The inspections can take time because crews must check the electrical system in each home. [WTIC News reported](https://www.audacy.com/wtic/news/local/east-hampton-power-surge-and-door-to-door-home-inspections) that residents were being asked to unplug equipment and remove lightbulbs from fixed fixtures while circuit panels were tested, a process that can take about an hour per house. The town identified Terp Road, higher-numbered addresses on Schoolhouse Lane and numbers 70 through 128 on Hog Hill Road as areas where residents should expect visits, according to WFSB.

Eversource said it was working to restore service to the 41 customers near Hog Hill Road while coordinating with town officials and residents. The company’s public statement did not give a restoration deadline. Town officials said small groups of homes could be reconnected after they were cleared, while some properties might need another inspection after power returned. That means the neighborhood may not come back online all at once.

Residents also received a warning about generators. Eversource asked people in the affected area to leave generators off until the wiring had been checked. That instruction matters because a generator connected to a damaged electrical system can create additional hazards for occupants and utility workers. Homeowners who believe equipment or wiring was damaged were told they could use an electrician and submit a claim to Eversource; the company’s position, as described by the town and [The Hour](https://www.thehour.com/news/article/east-hampton-power-surge-electrical-damage-22476288.php), is that internal wiring damage initially falls to the property owner while the claim is reviewed.

The incident is a different kind of outage from a storm-related line failure. In a conventional interruption, a utility can often repair the fault and re-energize a circuit after confirming that the outside network is safe. Here, the reported surge or back-feed may have reached equipment inside homes, so crews must account for conditions beyond the utility pole. The public reports do not yet say which component malfunctioned, how high the voltage rose or whether every affected house sustained damage.

For East Hampton residents, the next milestones are the completion of the house-by-house tests, a safe restoration schedule and clearer information about reimbursement. The town and Eversource were still investigating Wednesday, Oct. 14, and the available reports did not establish whether the event was isolated to the three named roads or whether additional customers could later be identified. Until inspections are complete, residents should follow the utility and local officials’ instructions about generators, electrical equipment and access for repair crews.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: East Hampton power surge leaves 41 homes awaiting inspections
seoDescription: Eversource and firefighters are inspecting 41 East Hampton homes after a possible power surge and suspected equipment malfunction.
